format_status.not_suggested: Not suggested for the detected shape
format_status.no_reverse: Reverse parse not supported for this format

jsonl.pretty_desc: Canonical JSONL is single-line. Enable for human-readable multi-line records.

csv.header_desc: Emit the first row as column names derived from object keys.
csv.nested_strategy_desc: How to handle nested objects/arrays inside cells.
csv.escape_formulae_desc: Prefix cells starting with = + - @ with ' so spreadsheet apps don't run them as formulas. Changes the data, so it's off by default.

xml.item_name_desc: Used for items when the root is an array. Object keys name their own array items.

toml.sort_keys_desc: Recursive — applies at every nesting level. Useful for stable diffs.
toml.null_handling_desc: TOML has no null. Omit drops null keys and array items; Error stops and shows where the null is.

markdown.escape_pipes_desc: Replace | with \| inside cell values so they don't break the table.

sql.multi_row_desc: Combine rows into a single INSERT statement per chunk.
sql.chunk_size_desc: Maximum rows per INSERT when multi-row is on.
sql.include_create_desc: Infer column types from every row and emit a CREATE TABLE statement.
sql.table_name_desc: Use schema.table for a qualified name (e.g. dbo.Users).

resx.comment_key_desc: When an entry is shaped as { value, _comment }, this key supplies the <comment> element.
resx.include_schema_desc: Visual Studio expects this. The required resheader entries are always written.
resx.sort_keys_desc: Useful for stable diffs across locale files.

bson.encoding_desc: How to render the binary BSON output as text. Downloads always contain raw bytes.

cbor.encoding_desc: How to render the binary CBOR output as text. Downloads always contain raw bytes.

msgpack.encoding_desc: How to render the binary MessagePack output as text. Downloads always contain raw bytes.

status.precision_hint: Integers beyond ±2^53 can't be represented exactly in JSON numbers and were rounded. Quote them as strings to keep every digit.

about.title: About JSONPrism
about.p1: JSONPrism takes a single JSON input and disperses it into many target formats — like white light through a prism — and parses six of them back. Conversion runs entirely on your device, so the data you paste or drop never leaves it.
about.p2: Built with React 19, TypeScript 7, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui. The web version is served by Cloudflare Workers; the desktop and Android apps are built with Tauri 2. Source on GitHub.

privacy.title: Your data
privacy.web: Conversion happens in your browser; files and text you paste are never uploaded. This website is hosted on Cloudflare, uses Turnstile for a quick human check, and counts anonymous page views with Cloudflare Web Analytics (no cookies) unless you turn it off under Appearance.
privacy.desktop: This desktop app works fully offline: no analytics, no human check, and no network requests except links you open yourself.
privacy.android: This Android app works fully offline: no analytics, no human check, and no network requests except links you open yourself.
